schema.frontmatter_field: type: string required: false default: directory name applicability: cli excerpt: | Display name for the skill. If omitted, uses the directory name. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (max 64 characters). caveats: - "Max 64 characters. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only." - "If omitted, the directory name is used as the slash-command name." - "Name collision resolution: enterprise > personal > project. Plugin skills use plugin-name:skill-name namespace." notes_for_skill: - "The subagent-builder skill should set this explicitly to control the /slash-command name." - "Name must be unique within the same priority level; conflicts resolved by priority tier." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: string required: false default: first paragraph of markdown content applicability: cli excerpt: | What the skill does and when to use it. Claude uses this to decide when to apply the skill. If omitted, uses the first paragraph of markdown content. Front-load the key use case: the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage. caveats: - "Combined description + when_to_use is capped at 1,536 characters in the skill listing." - "If disable-model-invocation is true, the description is NOT loaded into context — Claude never sees it." - "With user-invocable: false, the description IS in context but the user cannot invoke it from the / menu." - "Front-load the key use case since text gets truncated from the end." notes_for_skill: - "Critical for auto-invocation: Claude uses this field to decide when to load the skill automatically." - "For a subagent-builder skill, description should front-load trigger phrases like 'create a subagent', 'build an agent', 'add a subagent'." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: string required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Additional context for when Claude should invoke the skill, such as trigger phrases or example requests. Appended to `description` in the skill listing and counts toward the 1,536-character cap. caveats: - "Counts toward the shared 1,536-character cap with description — use sparingly." - "Appended to description in the skill listing; not a separate context window entry." notes_for_skill: - "Useful for listing alternate phrasings that trigger the skill (e.g. 'make an agent', 'set up a subagent')." - "Keep short since it eats into the description budget." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: string required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Hint shown during autocomplete to indicate expected arguments. Example: `[issue-number]` or `[filename] [format]`. caveats: - "Display only — does not enforce argument structure or count." notes_for_skill: - "Useful for documenting expected input format in the autocomplete menu." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: boolean required: false default: false values: [true, false] applicability: cli excerpt: | Set to `true` to prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill. Use for workflows you want to trigger manually with `/name`. Default: `false`.
`disable-model-invocation: true`: Only you can invoke the skill. Use this for workflows with side effects or that you want to control timing, like `/commit`, `/deploy`, or `/send-slack-message`. You don't want Claude deciding to deploy because your code looks ready. caveats: - "When true, the skill description is NOT loaded into Claude's context — Claude is unaware the skill exists." - "Per the invocation table: Description not in context, full skill loads only when the user invokes." - "The user-invocable field only controls menu visibility, not Skill tool access. Use disable-model-invocation: true to block programmatic invocation." notes_for_skill: - "A subagent-builder skill should set this to true if it has significant side effects (file creation in .claude/agents/)." - "If you want Claude to proactively suggest the skill, leave it false and rely on description matching." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Control who invokes a skill" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: boolean required: false default: true values: [true, false] applicability: cli excerpt: | Set to `false` to hide from the `/` menu. Use for background knowledge users shouldn't invoke directly. Default: `true`.
`user-invocable: false`: Only Claude can invoke the skill. Use this for background knowledge that isn't actionable as a command. A `legacy-system-context` skill explains how an old system works. Claude should know this when relevant, but `/legacy-system-context` isn't a meaningful action for users to take. caveats: - "Controls menu visibility only — does NOT block Claude's Skill tool access." - "To block Claude from invoking a skill, use disable-model-invocation: true instead." - "When false, description is still in context so Claude can find and load the skill automatically." notes_for_skill: - "A subagent-builder skill is intentionally user-invocable (user types /create-subagent or similar), so leave this true." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Control who invokes a skill" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: list required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Tools Claude can use without asking permission when this skill is active. Accepts a space-separated string or a YAML list.
The `allowed-tools` field grants permission for the listed tools while the skill is active, so Claude can use them without prompting you for approval. It does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable, and your permission settings still govern tools that are not listed. caveats: - "Grants permission for listed tools only while the skill is active — not a global permission change." - "Does NOT restrict other tools: every tool remains callable; unlisted tools still follow normal permission settings." - "Accepts space-separated string (e.g. 'Read Grep Bash(git *)') or YAML list format." - "To block tools, use deny rules in permission settings, not this field." notes_for_skill: - "A subagent-builder skill writing .claude/agents/ files will need Write and possibly Read pre-approved here." - "Example: allowed-tools: Read Write Bash(ls *)" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Pre-approve tools for a skill" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: string required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Model to use when this skill is active. caveats: - "Documented in the frontmatter reference table but no additional detail is provided in the source." notes_for_skill: - "Can be used to target a specific Claude model for this skill's execution." unknown_in_official_docs: true unknown_passage: | "Model to use when this skill is active." — No further detail on valid values, format, or interaction with context: fork / agent field is provided in this source. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: enum required: false default: inherits from session values: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max] applicability: cli excerpt: | Effort level when this skill is active. Overrides the session effort level. Default: inherits from session. Options: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; available levels depend on the model. caveats: - "Available effort levels depend on the active model — not all values apply to all models." - "Overrides the session-level effort setting for the duration of the skill." notes_for_skill: - "A subagent-builder skill may benefit from 'high' or 'xhigh' effort for thorough agent design." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: enum required: false default: none values: [fork] applicability: cli excerpt: | Set to `fork` to run in a forked subagent context.
Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent. It won't have access to your conversation history.
With `context: fork`, you write the task in your skill and pick an agent type to execute it. [...] The `agent` field determines the execution environment (model, tools, and permissions). caveats: - "context: fork only makes sense for skills with explicit instructions. If your skill contains guidelines like 'use these API conventions' without a task, the subagent receives the guidelines but no actionable prompt, and returns without meaningful output." - "The forked subagent does NOT have access to the main conversation history." - "The skill content becomes the subagent's task/prompt — not a system prompt." - "CLAUDE.md is loaded into the forked subagent context." notes_for_skill: - "Use context: fork when the skill should run independently (e.g. generating a subagent definition file without polluting main context)." - "Pairs with the agent field to control which agent type runs the task." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Run skills in a subagent" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: string required: false default: general-purpose applicability: cli excerpt: | Which subagent type to use when `context: fork` is set.
The `agent` field specifies which subagent configuration to use. Options include built-in agents (`Explore`, `Plan`, `general-purpose`) or any custom subagent from `.claude/agents/`. If omitted, uses `general-purpose`.
| Approach | System prompt | Task | Also loads | | Skill with `context: fork` | From agent type (`Explore`, `Plan`, etc.) | SKILL.md content | CLAUDE.md | caveats: - "Only meaningful when context: fork is also set. Has no effect without it." - "Built-in values: Explore, Plan, general-purpose." - "Also accepts any custom subagent name from .claude/agents/." - "If omitted, defaults to general-purpose." - "The agent type determines the system prompt, available tools, and permissions for the forked subagent." notes_for_skill: - "A subagent-builder skill running context: fork should specify agent: general-purpose (or a custom capable agent) since it needs Write tool access to create agent files." - "Explore agent is read-only optimized — avoid for skills that write files." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Run skills in a subagent" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: object required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Hooks scoped to this skill's lifecycle. See Hooks in skills and agents for configuration format. caveats: - "Configuration format is documented in the Hooks reference (/en/hooks#hooks-in-skills-and-agents), not in this source." notes_for_skill: - "Could be used to trigger post-processing after a subagent-builder skill creates an agent file (e.g. validate frontmatter)." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: list required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Glob patterns that limit when this skill is activated. Accepts a comma-separated string or a YAML list. When set, Claude loads the skill automatically only when working with files matching the patterns. Uses the same format as path-specific rules. caveats: - "Only restricts automatic activation — does not prevent manual /skill-name invocation." - "Accepts comma-separated string or YAML list." notes_for_skill: - "Not relevant for a general-purpose subagent-builder skill; leave unset so it can trigger in any project." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: enum required: false default: bash values: [bash, powershell] applicability: cli excerpt: | Shell to use for `` !`command` `` and ` ```! ` blocks in this skill. Accepts `bash` (default) or `powershell`. Setting `powershell` runs inline shell commands via PowerShell on Windows. Requires `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1`. caveats: - "powershell option requires CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1 environment variable." - "Only affects inline shell injection (!`command` and ```! blocks), not Bash tool calls." notes_for_skill: - "Leave as default (bash) for a cross-platform subagent-builder skill unless explicitly targeting Windows." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills section: "Frontmatter reference" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00
